$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json,
trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. Precedent for a per-repo port: kubelab,
hive and web each carry their own copy; the SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`. Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND when the question cannot be
computed, precisely so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear one. But a check
that reports the same thing every time it runs stops being read, which is how a gate degrades
into noise. Measured 2026-08-31, from the same reasoning kubelab recorded when it found its own
port had omitted `triage.marker`.
The `github-actions` entry below was ORIGINALLY omitted on the measurement that no
PR-Agent ran here. That measurement is superseded by this file's own history: the
workflow landed to end a 59 % decline rate on the vendor reviewer (17 of 29 recent PRs
carried `Review limit reached`), so the entry declares an actor that is about to exist
rather than one that was observed. Read the entry's own `why` for what has and has not
been verified, and treat the first run of pr-agent.yml as the check that makes it real.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. The first draft of this port carried dotfiles'
'No actionable comments were generated in the recent review', which is how a clean CodeRabbit run
attests over there. It appears in ZERO comments in this repository (searched across #293-#298,
#300, #301, #305, #306, #310, #311). A marker that never matches makes `prtriage.reviewOutput`
find no reviewer output, so the queue would report 'clear' on every PR forever -- the port would
have been silently dead, which is the exact failure this file exists to end. What CodeRabbit
actually emits in this repo, by PR:
## Walkthrough            -> #293 #298 #301 #310   (a review ran; this is the attesting marker)
## Review limit reached   -> #294 #295 #296 #300 #311  (also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai')
## Review skipped         -> #297                  (nothing reviewable in the selected files)
(no CodeRabbit output)    -> #292 #302 #303 #304   (dependabot; excluded from the workflow)
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.

reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles and kubelab registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change, and in this repo it is the normal case rather than the exception -- measured over #293..#311, five PRs (#294, #295, #296, #300, #311) drew 'Review limit reached' and one more (#297) drew 'Review skipped', so a decline that REFUSED would make the gate red more often than green and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer: a reviewer that could not run is not a reviewer that refused. LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED, because the two GitHub APIs disagree: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai. The dotfiles 'no complaints' review marker is deliberately NOT reused -- see the $comment on review_markers.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The marker is the `review` command's own heading. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports before being declared here — kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot] (spot-checked on #1500, #1362) and dotfiles has 172. It has NEVER been observed in ts-bridge, because this workflow has not run here: the first green run of pr-agent on a ts-bridge PR is the verification, and until then this entry is a declaration of intent, not of an actor.

triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`, so the writer and the reader are not a two-file agreement nobody checks. A disposition that lives only in a chat message evaporates, and the Definition of Done's Review item would then rest on a claim nobody can re-read. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message.

signatures.name: release-please
signatures.why: Measured on #287: exactly these two paths. Matched by DIFF SIGNATURE with set equality, never by author or branch — release-please runs under a human PAT here, so an author rule would not fire, and a branch rule would let any branch named to match walk past the gate. The moment such a PR touches one more file the exemption stops applying, and it stops applying just as surely if one declared file is not touched. This is not 'small PRs need no review': a release commit mechanically restates commits that were each reviewed when they landed, and reporting `declined` on it says something false.
